claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its high-entropy-alloy derivatives have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe.
Annealing FeCoNi-based alloys at 500–700 °C for 1–10 hours will induce precipitation of a Co-rich secondary phase.
The precipitated Co-rich phase will have a high magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant.
A secondary phase with high magnetocrystalline anisotropy can act as a domain-wall pinning site.
Domain-wall pinning increases the energy required for domain-wall motion.
Increasing the energy required for domain-wall motion increases coercive field.
Co-rich-phase precipitation will increase coercive field by at least a factor of five relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a derivative.
The hypothesis is intended to apply to FeCoNi-based alloys whose compositions deviate by no more than 10% from equiatomic FeCoNi.
The post-intervention structural scope is an fcc matrix containing a thermally precipitated secondary phase.
The predicted coercivity change is defined for magnetic measurements performed at room temperature.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement may depend on annealing conditions, composition, and microstructure.
